title: Frame In, Frame Out: Measuring Framing Bias in LLM-Generated News Summaries

live_model.evidence: Sec. 2: "...a three-member LLM jury comprising GPT-4.1-nano, GPT-4o, and GPT-3.5-Turbo. Each model independently labels a summary as Framed or Not Framed"

prompt.location: Sec. 2 (jury-labeling prompt referenced as "the best-performing prompt from Pastorino et al. (2026)", not reprinted in this paper)
prompt.note: Framing-jury prompt is cited from a companion paper rather than printed here.

claim.metric: none individually for gpt-4.1-nano (jury majority vote is reported only in aggregate; headline framing rates in the paper belong to the 27 summarization subject models, not to the jury members)

data.source: XSum dataset; FIFO benchmark released at github.com/vpastorino/FIFO

notes: GPT-4.1-nano is one of three jury models that LABEL other models' summaries for framing; it is not one of the 27 summarization models under study, so no headline number is attributable to it as a subject. Jury-vs-expert agreement (Cohen's kappa 0.616) is reported only for the combined 3-model jury, not per model.
